reference_drawer.title: Transposition Reference Guide
reference_drawer.description: Move one term at a time and preserve equality:

items.rule: A term added on one side is subtracted when moved to the other side.
items.formula: x + a = b \Rightarrow x = b - a

items.rule: A term subtracted on one side is added when moved to the other side.
items.formula: x - a = b \Rightarrow x = b + a

items.rule: Divide both sides by a non-zero coefficient to isolate the variable.
Whatever operation is performed on one side must be performed on the other side.
items.formula: a = b \Rightarrow a + k = b + k

concepts.title: 1. Equality and inverse operations
concepts.subtitle: Keep both sides balanced
concepts.summary: An equation remains true when the same operation is applied to both sides.

points.text: Addition is undone by subtraction, and multiplication is undone by division.
Write one operation per notebook line.

concepts.formula: a = b \Rightarrow a - k = b - k
concepts.trap: Do not change a sign by memory without applying the inverse operation to both sides.

concepts.title: 2. Transpose one term
concepts.subtitle: Move terms with the opposite operation
concepts.summary: When a term crosses the equality sign, its operation changes to its inverse.

points.text: From x + 3 = 9, subtract 3 to obtain x = 9 - 3.
The constant 9 does not move in this line; only 3 is transposed.

concepts.formula: x + a = b \Rightarrow x = b - a
concepts.trap: Never transpose both terms in one step when the question asks for a single atomic operation.

concepts.title: 3. Isolate the coefficient
concepts.subtitle: Divide only after collecting terms
concepts.summary: After the variable term is alone on one side, divide by its coefficient.

points.text: From -2y = -6, divide both sides by -2 to get y = 3.
Dividing by a negative keeps the answer positive when both signs are negative.

concepts.trap: Do not divide one term only; divide the entire side by the coefficient.

concepts.title: 4. Transposing fractions
concepts.subtitle: Use reciprocals and common denominators
concepts.summary: A fractional coefficient is undone by multiplying by its reciprocal, while a fractional constant is moved with its inverse operation.

points.text: Reciprocal: The reciprocal of 3/4 is 4/3, so multiply both sides by 4/3.
Exactness: Keep fractions exact; convert to a decimal only when the answer requires it.

concepts.trap: Do not divide by a fraction by dividing its numerator only; multiply by the complete reciprocal.
